content.title: About
content.content: Carrots are a root vegetable from the Apiaceae family, cultivated worldwide. Cooked carrots have a tender texture, a mildly sweet flavor, and a bright orange color due to their high beta‑carotene content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beta‑carotene in carrots is converted to vitamin A, essential for vision.
Carrots come in many colors: orange, yellow, purple, red, and white.
They are believed to boost immunity thanks to antioxidant compounds.
In the 17th century carrots were mostly purple; the orange variety was developed in the Netherlands.

items.title: Supports vision
items.content: Vitamin A derived from beta‑carotene is crucial for retinal health and night vision.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Carotenoids and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune system support
items.content: B‑vitamins and minerals contribute to normal immune function.

items.title: Cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium and dietary fiber aid in blood pressure regulation and cholesterol balance.

items.title: Digestive health
items.content: Fiber promotes intestinal motility and regular bowel movements.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to carrots.

items.title: Excess beta‑carotene
items.content: Very high intake can cause carotenemia – a temporary yellowing of the skin.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic carrots, wash them thoroughly to remove possible chemical residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked carrots can be served as a side dish, added to salads, soups, purees, or incorporated into casseroles. A drizzle of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and fresh herbs enhance their flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked carrots in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer keeping, freeze them in portions.

coffee-iced-latte-decaffeinated-with-non.title: Coffee, Iced Latte, Decaffeinated, with Non‑Dairy Milk

content.title: About
content.content: Decaffeinated iced latte is a refreshing beverage made from espresso that has had the caffeine removed and a smooth non‑dairy milk (soy, almond, oat, etc.). Served over ice, it offers a mild coffee aroma and creamy texture, ideal for those avoiding caffeine or dairy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeination is usually done by water or CO₂ methods, preserving most flavor compounds.
Non‑dairy milks add their own flavor notes: oat is slightly sweet, almond is nutty, soy is neutral.
Iced lattes are often topped with plant‑based whipped cream and a sprinkle of cinnamon or cocoa powder.
In many countries, decaf coffee has become popular among pregnant women and caffeine‑sensitive individuals.
The word “latte” comes from the Italian “latte,” meaning “milk.”

items.title: Reduced caffeine load
items.content: The lack of caffeine makes the drink safe for people sensitive to stimulants and for pregnant individuals.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and support heart health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Even after decaffeination, coffee retains vitamins B2 and B3, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Non‑dairy milks are often fortified with probiotics and fiber, promoting a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low‑calorie option
items.content: When unsweetened and made with low‑fat plant milk, the drink is low in calories, suitable for weight management.

items.title: Allergy to plant ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to soy, almond, or oat milk.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Pre‑made versions are often sweetened; check the label and choose unsweetened options when possible.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: Certain brands add flavorings and preservatives that may be undesirable for sensitive consumers.

content.title: How to Enjoy
content.content: Serve the iced latte in a tall glass over ice, optionally add a touch of sweetener, cinnamon, or cocoa powder. Mixing different plant milks can create unique flavor profiles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared beverage refrigerated and consume within 24 hours. Store opened plant‑based milk according to the manufacturer’s instructions, usually in the fridge.

content.title: About
content.content: Iced latte is a cold coffee beverage made with espresso, nonfat milk, and flavorings (such as vanilla or caramel). It is served over ice and has a light, creamy texture without fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Iced latte originated in Japan in the 1980s as a variation of the traditional latte.
Nonfat milk retains most of the protein while containing almost no fat, making the drink lower in calories.
Flavorings are often added as syrups, which can be natural or artificial.
Coffee for iced latte is frequently prepared as cold brew or quickly chilled espresso to preserve aroma.
In some countries the drink is topped with a sprinkle of cinnamon or cocoa powder.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Caffeine improves focus and increases alertness.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Nonfat milk reduces the overall calorie content of the beverage.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Despite being fat‑free, nonfat milk still provides calcium important for bone health.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Caffeine can slightly raise metabolic rate, aiding calorie burning.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat after caffeine.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Flavored syrups often contain significant sugar, increasing the drink’s calories.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Coffee can irritate the stomach in people with high acidity.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Those with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy should use alternative milks.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve iced latte in tall glasses over ice, add flavorings to taste. It can be garnished with nonfat whipped cream or a dusting of cinnamon. For a lighter version, use unsweetened syrups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared beverage should be kept refrigerated and consumed within 24 hours. Nonfat milk should be stored at 0‑4 °C and used within 5‑7 days after opening.
